title: The Rope Bridge
pageTitle: Determine Distance on the Coordinate Plane
covers: how to find the distance between two points on a horizontal or vertical line of the coordinate plane with absolute value: subtract when the points are on the same side of zero, add when they are on opposite sides
cert: finding horizontal and vertical distances on the coordinate plane with absolute value

intro.caption: Lesson 7-6 — distance on the coordinate plane. Floor −7 of the dungeon is split by a deep chasm. The bridge is gone. Only the posts are left, and Sol's map shows exactly where each post stands.

balloons.t: Each post is a point on my map. To fix the bridge, we cut each rope to the distance between two posts.
Measure twice, cut once! And Kwame, please do not cut anything yet.
Posts at (2, 5) and (2, 1). I added: 5 + 1 = 6. So I cut 6 units! Why am I in the slime?
Both y's are positive. Same side of zero! Subtract: 5 − 1 = 4.

pages.caption: Kwame's rope was 2 units too long. When two points are on the same side of an axis, the distance is the difference of the absolute values.

balloons.t: These two posts are both left of zero. Same side again, so no adding!
This post is at (−5, 2). The far post is at (4, 2). The chasm is right in the middle.
One post is left of zero, one is right. Walk to zero, then keep walking!
Health check: Kwame, 1 slime bath. Rule check: look at the signs FIRST. Same sign, subtract. Opposite signs, add.
So I pick the tool before I cut. Got it.
Fresh rope! I always ADD, so you get more rope. More rope, more gold!
Next time, I measure first. Probably.
Tight ropes, dry feet. Even Kwame's!

win.caption: Distance is never negative. On a horizontal or vertical line, look at the coordinate that changes. Same side of zero: subtract the absolute values. Opposite sides: add them.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Same Side
gates.prompt: Both posts sit on the same side of zero. Cut the rope to the right length, then set a new post.
hints: Conceptual: when both coordinates have the same sign, one point is farther from zero than the other. The rope only covers the extra part.
Procedural: find the coordinate that changes. Take both absolute values, then subtract the smaller from the larger.

steps: Practice posts: (1, 7) and (1, 3). The x's match, so the rope is vertical. Look at the y's.
Both y's are positive, so both posts are above zero. Same side: subtract.

items.label: (−6, −1) to (−2, −1) =
items.aria: units of rope between the posts at negative 6, negative 1 and negative 2, negative 1

fb.msg: That's 6 + 2. Both x's are negative, so both posts are on the same side of zero. Adding counts the stretch from 0 to −2 twice. Subtract.
Distance is never negative. Use absolute values: |−6| − |−2| = 6 − 2.
The y's match, so the rope is horizontal. Look at the x's, −6 and −2. They are not the same.

items.fbDefault: Find the x's, take their absolute values, and subtract the smaller from the larger.

items.q: A new post goes straight down from (1, 4), and the rope is 3 units long. Tap where the new post goes.

fb.msg: That moves 3 units right. The rope goes straight down, so x stays 1 and y changes.
That post is 4 + 3 = 7 units below (1, 4). Start at y = 4 and count down only 3.
That's only 1 unit down. Count 3 units down from y = 4.

items.fbDefault: Start at (1, 4). Keep x = 1 and count 3 units down.

gates.pass: The first rope is cut to 4 units and fits post to post. Kwame watches with his hands in his pockets.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Opposite Sides
gates.prompt: The main bridge crosses zero: one post on each side of the chasm. How long is each rope?
hints: Conceptual: when the signs are opposite, the rope goes from one post to zero AND from zero to the other post. Both parts count.
Procedural: find the coordinate that changes. Take both absolute values and add them.

steps: Practice posts: (−2, 5) and (3, 5). The y's match, so the rope is horizontal. Look at the x's.
−2 is left of zero and 3 is right of zero. Opposite sides: add.

items.label: (−5, 2) to (4, 2) =
items.aria: units of rope across the chasm from negative 5, 2 to 4, 2

fb.msg: That's 5 − 4. The posts are on opposite sides of zero, so you need the part to zero AND the part after zero. Add.
That's −5 + 4. Distance is never negative. Use absolute values: 5 and 4.
Right size, wrong sign. Distance is never negative: 9 units.

items.fbDefault: Count from −5 to 0, then from 0 to 4, and add the two parts.

items.q: A rope hangs straight down from (−2, 3), crosses the x-axis, and is 5 units long. Tap the post at the bottom.

fb.msg: That post is 3 + 3 = 6 units away. You need 5: 3 units down to zero, then only 2 more.
That's 3 + 5 = 8 units away. The 5 units start at y = 3, not at zero.
That moves 5 units right. The rope hangs straight down, so x stays −2.
Right height, wrong side. The rope hangs straight down, so x stays −2, not 2.

items.fbDefault: Start at (−2, 3). Count 3 down to the x-axis, then 2 more.

gates.pass: Nine units of rope stretch across the gap, and the hanging rope reaches (−2, −2). The bridge starts to look like a bridge.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Choose the Tool
gates.prompt: Before you cut, choose the tool: add or subtract? Look at the signs first.
hints: Conceptual: first find which coordinate changes. Then ask: are the two points on the same side of zero, or on opposite sides?
Procedural: same sign → subtract the absolute values. Opposite signs → add the absolute values. The answer is never negative.

steps: Practice: (5, −2) and (5, −6). The x's match, so look at the y's.
−2 and −6 are both negative. Same side of zero, so subtract.

items.q: Posts at (−4, −6) and (−4, −1). Which is right?

options.fb: Both y's are negative, so both posts are below the x-axis. Adding would measure from −6 all the way up to +1.
Distance is never negative. Subtract the smaller absolute value from the larger: 6 − 1.
The x's match, so the rope is vertical. Use the y-coordinates, not the x's.

items.q: Kwame says the distance from (−3, 4) to (5, 4) is 2, because 5 − 3 = 2. Is he right?

options.t: Yes. Always subtract the absolute values.
options.fb: Subtract only when the points are on the same side. −3 and 5 have opposite signs.

options.t: No. It is 9, because there are 9 grid lines from −3 to 5.
options.fb: Count the jumps, not the lines. From −3 to 5 there are 8 jumps.
The size is right, but distance is never negative.

gates.pass: Subtract for same side, add for opposite sides. Kwame writes it on his shield in big letters.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Grimble's Rope Shop
gates.prompt: The last bridge has three posts: A (−5, 4), B (3, 4) and C (3, −2). Grimble always adds. You measure for real.
hints: Conceptual: for each rope, find the coordinate that changes and check the signs. Grimble's adding only works for opposite sides.
Procedural: A to B is horizontal (look at x). B to C is vertical (look at y). Then count steps from C for the last post.

steps: Practice bridge: P (−1, 6) to Q (4, 6) to R (4, 2).
P to Q: x goes from −1 to 4, opposite sides, so 1 + 4 = 5 units.
Q to R: y goes from 6 to 2, same side, so 6 − 2 = 4 units.
worked.q: How far is R (4, 2) from S (−3, 2)?

items.label: Rope 1 · A (−5, 4) to B (3, 4):
items.aria: units of rope from A to B

fb.msg: That's 5 − 3. A is left of zero and B is right of zero, so add.
That's −5 + 3. Use absolute values, and remember distance is never negative.

items.fbDefault: The y's match. Look at x: −5 and 3 are on opposite sides of zero.

items.label: Rope 2 · B (3, 4) to C (3, −2):
items.aria: units of rope from B to C

fb.msg: That's 4 − 2. B is above the x-axis and C is below it. Opposite sides, so add.
The x's are both 3, so the rope is vertical. Use the y's: 4 and −2.

items.fbDefault: The x's match. Look at y: 4 and −2 are on opposite sides of zero.

items.q: Grimble's last post D is 4 units left of C (3, −2). Tap where D goes.

fb.msg: Right x, wrong sign on y. D stays level with C, so y is still −2.
Those are swapped. x comes first: D is at x = −1, y = −2.
That moves 4 units down. Left means the x changes: 3 − 4.
That's 7 units left of C. Start at x = 3 and count only 4 left.

items.fbDefault: Start at C (3, −2). Keep y = −2 and count 4 units left.

gates.pass: SNIP, SNIP, SNIP. Eight units, six units, and D at (−1, −2). Grimble counts his leftover rope and sighs.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-6 — what the rope bridge taught us
rows: How far apart two points are. It is never negative, so a rope is never −4 units long.
(−6, −1) and (−2, −1) are both left of zero. |−6| − |−2| = 6 − 2 = 4 units.
(−5, 2) and (4, 2) are on both sides of zero. |−5| + |4| = 5 + 4 = 9 units.
Adding (2, 5) and (2, 1) gave 6, a rope 2 units too long. Check the signs before you pick add or subtract.
journal.quote: "Measure the gap, not the whole cave." — Pip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-6 (Determine Distance on the Coordinate Plane) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: horizontal and vertical distance between two points with absolute value, subtracting for points on the same side of zero and adding for points on opposite sides.
standards: Solve problems by graphing points in all four quadrants; use coordinates and absolute value to find distances
